scope: Source audit of preprocessing, base feature building, weekly context, round1 methods, temporal ranker, event model and v4/v5 exports; saved-artifact consistency checks; no training/full raw-data rebuild

cases.case: macro mean includes empty truth user

findings.requirement: section5: give the same fallback everywhere
findings.finding: Initial 180-second models and advanced >30%-history systems use differently ordered popularity fallback lists and different cold cohorts. This is disclosed by the report, and the original required-method comparison is internally controlled, but the cross-family strict table does not literally use the same fallback.
findings.recommendation: Add a clearly labelled no-refit harmonized evaluation using one frozen common fallback for all methods, or acknowledge this remaining strict-requirement gap. Preserve submitted v4 predictions/provenance.
findings.resolution: Both common-fallback and exact-matched-per-user-pool comparisons completed without fitting. Primary audit comparison in matched_pool_comparison.json uses the identical original v3 shortlist for all8, union12 cold users, and one shared 180s popularity list (verified present in every pool). Original submitted files and source scores unchanged. Updated examples included for consistent report use.

findings.finding: Strict targets use MAX stored fragments after the artificial May18 preprocessing split. Continuous sessions crossing that split can be undercounted for later/full-history queries; report explicitly discloses it. Replay features use raw sessions, not those fragments.
findings.recommendation: Keep limitation; do not claim exact official labels.

findings.finding: Repeated use of overlapping main/later holdouts causes selection optimism; temporal inner stopping avoids direct outer model fit but not research-level selection bias.
